_what: The post-migrate assertion pass re-runs every `do $$` block of every migration against the database the WHOLE set built, in lexical order, each in its own transaction that is rolled back. A block written when its batch was applied can be made false by a LATER batch that legitimately changes what it asserted; such a block is listed here, beside the later file(s) that changed it and a final-state replacement that restates EVERY assertion of the block as it stands at the end of the set. The replacement runs in the block's place.
_guards: Three, enforced by scripts/db/run.mjs on every `make db-migrate-clean`: (1) a block NOT listed here must pass as written; (2) a block listed here must still FAIL as written, with SQLSTATE P0001 and a message beginning with the entry's `fails_with` (its own raise at the recorded conflict, not a syntax error and not a new failure earlier in the block), or the entry is stale and the pass fails; (3) the replacement must pass. A migration that makes an earlier block false therefore fails migrate-clean until the same change adds an entry here -- changing another batch's guarantee is a reviewable line in the diff, never a side effect. A `fails_with` runs past a raise's first `%` only when that argument is declared `integer` (a count, which is deterministic); a text argument is a list whose order Postgres does not fix, so the entry stops before it: the first version of 120's entry included the first of two policy names, the order of which Postgres does not fix, and main's CI run 36311266393 received them the other way round and reported the entry stale although the block failed exactly as recorded.
_editing: Migrations are never edited (migration invariant 1). Replacements are not migrations and are edited when a later batch supersedes them again. Each `SUPERSEDED BY` comment inside a replacement names the later file that made that change necessary; everything else in the replacement is the original block word for word.
